correctness.rationale: The degree-n parity-symmetric Chebyshev polynomial Q has n-2 sign-alternating roots via T_(n-1) grid. The at-most-two remaining roots are either real or pure imaginary. Positive imaginary roots are classified uniquely by strictly increasing hyperbolic ratios with sharp endpoint ratios. The odd-degree intermediate interval is resolved by Q'(0) sign and another symmetric real-root pair; at equality degree exhaustion establishes exactly triple origin, and at p=1/2 the known factorization gives the even double root. Cosine composition is locally invertible over every root because Q(±1)≠0; two lifts per polynomial zero yield complete entire zero counts. Analytic expansions give the square-root laws. The embedded checker confirmed 46 exact Sturm counts, 48 Fourier/Chebyshev evaluations, and 15 symbolic parameter identities; finite tests do not establish the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The four-atom positive probability measure is a canonical minimal nontrivial two-radius symmetric discrete Fourier model. The theorem completely determines all its complex Fourier zeros uniformly in degree and mass, showing exactly four nonreal zeros per period when the threshold is crossed and a parity-sensitive double/triple collision with explicit imaginary height. The nontrivial finite odd-degree real-root window differs from the older fixed-coefficient asymptotic zero theorem. The result is an all-order natural classification, not an arbitrary isolated example or a rebranding of the known equal-weight factorization.
